summary: Lewis Lancaster works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a BA at Roanoke College, an MTh at Claremont School of Theology, and a PhD at UW–Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He held long posts at UC Berkeley and the University of the West.

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

A scholar of Tibetology, Lhagpa Phuntshogs served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center starting in 2000.
Liang Cai specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an attested post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas in 2014.
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Lili Zheng studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Lilian Silburn studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo. She held appointments at the CNRS from around 1947 to 1974.
Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under M. Sri Rammandala and Julius Berugoda, and held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya (attested in 1970 and 2008).
A philosopher, Lin He studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from circa 1919 to 1926. He later held an academic post at National Tsing Hua University from around 1931 to 1937.
Specializing in Indology, Lin Heng earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

Linda Hogan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Maynooth and Trinity College Dublin (PhD 1991). She taught at Chester and Leeds, and later served as Chair of Ecumenics and Vice-Provost (2011–2016) at Trinity College Dublin.
A scholar of religious studies and Indology, Linda Jean LaMacchia earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Her studies include doctoral supervision by Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentoring by Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned a PhD from Columbia University in 1993 and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune, working in Tibetology and religious studies, completed an MA under Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007) and studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark, specializing in sinology and other fields, served as a professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
A scholar in sinology, Ling Ji completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Linnart Mäll specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1965–1972), later holding a post at Tartu from circa 1969 to 2010.

Indologist Lionel David Barnett studied at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), was Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and lectured at SOAS (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia works in religious and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD at Lille University of Science and Technology (1997), he held posts at Lille 3 (attested 2002), EPHE, INALCO, KU Leuven, and Lumière University Lyon 2 (attested 2010–2014).

Liqian Liu specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council translation administration department (~1952–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1979).
